collection.description: You'll carry some of my years with it. Should a villager take the line, or politely say no?

ask.text:
(elder), the eldest villager, has a face so lined that the children say it's a map. (elder) says it is: every line is a place (elder.he/she) has been and a thing (elder.he/she) has learned. Today (elder.he/she) offers to give (subject) one of (elder.his/her) lines, the one that holds the way to the best fishing grounds, which (elder.he/she) has never told anyone.
"It'll cost you, mind," (elder) says. "Lines aren't free. You'll carry some of my years with it." Should (subject) take the line, or politely say no?

c1o1.text: In the morning, (subject)'s face is lined, (subject.his/her) hair is grey at the temples, and (subject.his/her) knees ache like an old fisher's. Ten years in a night. But (subject.he/she) knows, as clearly as (subject.his/her) own name, the way to the fishing grounds: the bend in the reef, the colour of the water, the bird that circles there. (subject.He/She) comes home with the canoe full.

c1o2.text: In the morning, (subject)'s face has a long new line down it, and several more besides, but (subject.his/her) body is as young as yesterday. "I gave you the line, not the years," (elder) says, looking pleased. "You're lucky. My grandmother gave me hers and the knees with it." The fishing grounds are exactly where (subject.he/she) said.

c1.text: (elder) puts (subject.his/her) thumb on (subject)'s forehead and draws it slowly down, the way a person draws in the sand. It feels warm, then heavy...

c2o1.text: (elder) never tells anyone else about the fishing grounds. When (elder.he/she) dies, years later, (subject) remembers the offer, and wonders. Then (subject.he/she) goes out in the canoe and starts looking, line by line, the way (elder) must have done, and finds the place at last when (subject.his/her) own face is lined. "Earned it," (subject.he/she) says to nobody.

text_only.reason: the word in the owner's story; what changes in the game is the ending's own EFFECT line (the ledger), so this word alone changes nothing

c2o2.text: "Good answer," says (elder). "Here's something for free, then." And (elder.he/she) talks for an hour, not about fishing, but about (subject)'s own work, things (elder.he/she) has noticed watching (subject) over the years: what (subject) does well, what (subject) does badly, and why. It is the most useful hour of advice (subject) has ever had.

c2.text: "Thank you," says (subject), "but I'd like to earn my own lines." (elder) laughs, a dry laugh like leaves, and pats (subject.his/her) hand...
